stem: Ines Duarte registered for the CFA Level I exam two months ago and works as a trainee at the fictional Kestrel Bank. Regarding the Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct, Ines is:
options: Not yet bound, because only charterholders are subject to them
Bound only after she passes Level I
Already bound, because candidates are subject to them from enrolment
explanation: The Code and Standards apply to all members and to all candidates in the CFA Program, starting when they enrol.

rationale.A: Incorrect. The framework applies to members and candidates, not only to charterholders.
rationale.B: Incorrect. There is no waiting period tied to passing an exam; candidates are bound from enrolment.
rationale.C: Correct. Enrolment as a candidate is enough to be bound by the Code and Standards.

stem: A portfolio manager at the fictional Halcyon Trust buys shares for her own account before executing a large client order in the same stock. The Standard most directly concerned with this conduct falls under:
explanation: Trading ahead of clients is addressed by the priority of transactions requirement, which sits within Standard VI, Conflicts of Interest.

rationale.A: Correct. Priority of transactions, which requires client trades to come before personal trades, is part of Standard VI on conflicts of interest.
rationale.B: Incorrect. Duties to employers covers loyalty to the employer, additional compensation and supervision, not the ordering of personal and client trades.
rationale.C: Incorrect. Integrity of capital markets covers material nonpublic information and manipulation; front-running a client is primarily a priority-of-transactions issue.

stem: After an investigation, CFA Institute professional conduct staff propose a one-year suspension for Dario Lund, a fictional charterholder. Dario believes he did nothing wrong. Which of the following is most accurate?
options: The proposed sanction is final once staff issue it
Dario may reject the proposed sanction, and the matter is then referred to a hearing panel
Dario may appeal only to a national securities regulator
explanation: A member or candidate can accept or reject a proposed sanction. If rejected, a hearing panel of volunteers from the disciplinary review committee decides whether a violation occurred and what sanction, if any, applies.

rationale.A: Incorrect. A proposal from staff is not final; the individual has the right to reject it.
rationale.B: Correct. Rejection sends the case to a hearing panel for an independent determination.
rationale.C: Incorrect. The Professional Conduct Program is a self-regulatory process; the next step after rejection is a hearing panel, not an outside regulator.

stem: Which statement best describes the relationship between the Code of Ethics and the Standards of Professional Conduct?
options: The Standards are broad aspirations, while the Code sets out detailed rules for specific situations
The Code applies to members, while the Standards apply only to candidates
The Code states broad ethical principles, and the Standards set out more specific obligations that put those principles into practice
explanation: The Code is a short set of principles; the Standards are organised into seven areas with sub-sections that specify required conduct. Both apply to members and candidates.

rationale.A: Incorrect. This reverses the roles: the Code is the broad layer and the Standards are the specific layer.
rationale.B: Incorrect. Both the Code and the Standards apply to members and candidates alike.
rationale.C: Correct. The Code provides principles and the Standards make them concrete and testable.
